summary: Tampalawela Dhammaratana specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Sunethradevi Pirivena, the University of Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and completed postdoctoral studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology who earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University. He served at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, and the Institute of Chinese Studies.

Tan Poh Beng works in Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, and also studied under Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Tan Sitong was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Renshan Yang from circa 1896 to 1898 and under Wang Zhengyi.

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at institutions including Hunan Normal University and Chuanshan Academy, taught at Lida Academy, and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University from circa 1937 to 1968.
Tanaya Afroz is a linguistics scholar who has been a research scholar or fellow at The Asiatic Society and studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya.
Tancredi Padova works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He has pursued doctoral studies and held a post at the University of Chicago.
Tandin Dorji is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He has served as a history lecturer at Sherubtse College and as a lecturer at the National Institute of Education, Paro.
Tanero Sasakawa was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896 and held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University.

Tansen Sen works in history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding faculty appointments at Baruch College (1997–2017) and NYU Shanghai (from 2017).
Tanso Hirose was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku from circa 1797 to 1801, studied under Hōdō, and founded Kangien in 1801.

Tanuja Ajotikar specializes in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. She has held posts at Harvard University, the Sanskrit Library as Assistant Professor, and Maharishi Vedic University as Co-Director of India Programs.

Tanzan Hara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He held appointments at the Ministry of Religion, the University of Tokyo, the Japan Academy, and Komazawa University.
Tao Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Ph.D. at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2017–2026) and was a postdoctoral fellow at Fo Guang Shan in 2026.

Tao Jiang works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and served as Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University.
Tao Jin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned a BA from Fudan University and a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.
Tapas Khanra is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who earned a Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay in 2021 and held a post there.
Tara Doyle is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who served at Emory University as a lecturer in religious studies, director of the Tibetan Studies Program, and later as Professor Emerita.
Tarapada Chowdhury was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Patna College, succeeding Edward Hamilton Johnston by 1950.
